summary_en.motivation: To understand the columnar-to-equiaxed transition in Al-Mg-Sc-Zr alloys during selective laser melting.

summary_en.result: Identified synergistic effects of composition and processing on grain refinement.
summary_en.validation: Validated only by metallography and EBSD; no mechanical testing performed.

papers.title: The three-prong method: a novel assessment of residual stress in laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Residual stress is a major problem for most metal-based laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) components. Residual stress can be reduced by appropriate build planning and post-process heat treatments; however, it is not always avoidable and can lead to build failures due to distortion and cracking. Accurate measurement of residual stress levels can be difficult due to high equipment set-up costs and long processing times. This paper introduces a simple but novel method of measuring residual stresses via a three-pronged cantilever component, the three-prong method (TPM). The method allows for a quick and easy characterisation of residual stress for a wide range of machine parameters, build strategies and materials. Many different cantilever designs have been used to indicate residual stress within additive manufacturing techniques. All of which share the same shortcoming that they indicate stress in one direction. If the principal component of stress is not aligned with the beam geometry, it will underestimate peak stress values. A novel three-prong design is proposed which covers two dimensions by utilising three adjoined cantilever beams, a configuration which echoes that of hole-drilling where three measurements are used to calculate the stress field around a drilled hole. Each arm of the component resembles a curved bridge-like structure; one end of each bridge is cut away from the base plate leaving the centre intact. Deformation of the beams is then measured using a co-ordinate measurement machine. Stress profiles are then estimated using finite element analysis by meshing the deflected structure and forcing it back to its original shape. In this paper, the new TPM is used to compare the residual stress levels of components built in Ti–6Al–4V with different hatch patterns, powers and exposure times.

summary_zh.motivation: 提出一种简单快速的LPBF残余应力测量方法
summary_zh.method: 设计三叉戟悬臂梁构件，通过变形测量和有限元反推应力
summary_zh.result: 成功比较不同工艺参数下的残余应力水平
summary_zh.validation: 通过坐标测量机测量变形并结合有限元分析验证

summary_en.motivation: To develop a simple and rapid method for measuring residual stress in laser powder bed fusion components.
summary_en.method: A three-pronged cantilever design is proposed, where deformation of the beams is measured and used to estimate stress profiles via finite element analysis.
summary_en.result: The method effectively compares residual stress levels under different hatch patterns, powers, and exposure times in Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed by coordinate measurement machine deformation measurements and finite element analysis.

summary_en.motivation: Heterogeneous data structures in multi-fidelity modeling hinder model accuracy and applicability.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian process-based multi-fidelity method is proposed to cope with diverse data structures such as grids and point clouds.
summary_en.result: The method demonstrates improved fusion capability and prediction accuracy on several numerical benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed using standard numerical functions and engineering case studies.

papers.title: Privacy of Personal Things in Active Learning Spaces Need Individually Evolved Requirements
papers.abstract: Technology-enhanced active learning (TEAL) spaces could represent a significant benefit to learning and teaching at universities. TEAL spaces support students in projecting presentations (e.g. from smart-phones) and sharing notes (e.g. from smart-watches) with peers. Importantly, this sharing is partly amongst their co-present small group but sometimes to the whole class. However, plugging personal things into smart spaces whose first requirement is to accept as many devices as possible is not without consequence. A projected notification of a political conversation, for example, has the potential to harm the individual both within the space and beyond, opening them to unwanted judgment, criticism and assessment.

summary_en.motivation: The paper investigates privacy risks associated with personal devices in technology-enhanced active learning spaces.
summary_en.method: It analyzes the consequences of plugging personal devices into smart spaces that prioritize device acceptance.
summary_en.result: The study highlights potential harm from unintended sharing of personal information in such environments.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; the paper is a conceptual discussion.
